saml.description: The SAML connector does not issue refresh tokens and ignores offline_access.
saml.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token as a freshness bug for SAML logins.

saml.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and stable.
saml.note: Differences in email or username attributes alone do not imply a principal change if NameID is unchanged.

saml.description: Dex requires sending the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML response InResponseTo value.
saml.note: Unsolicited or out-of-flow SAMLResponses failing are expected behavior.

saml.description: Dex requires an SP-initiated AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo rather than accepting unprompted AuthnResponses.
saml.note: A bare posted SAMLResponse without a preceding Dex auth flow should fail by design.

saml.description: When allowedGroups is configured, Dex filters authentication and optionally prunes non-allowed groups when filterGroups is true.
saml.note: Reduced groups in resulting claims may be intentional connector filtering, not privilege corruption.

saml.constraint: Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow at GET /auth and let Dex issue an AuthnRequest, then submit the forged SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id} with a matching InResponseTo. Unprompted SAMLResponses are rejected by design because Dex validates InResponseTo.

For SAML I1 signature-validation default tests, Dex documentation explicitly exposes insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true as a config option and warns it should only be used for testing. A valid insecure-default test MUST distinguish default behavior from this explicit opt-out; do NOT treat acceptance under insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true as a vulnerability.

For SAML issuer-validation tests, configure ssoIssuer when testing issuer mismatch. If ssoIssuer is unset, Dex may not enforce the expected Issuer value from the SAML response, so an issuer-mismatch result is uninterpretable as an I1 failure versus missing configuration.

For SAML audience-validation tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is configured, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST align forged Audience values with whichever of entityIssuer or redirectURI is active, or wrong-audience/no-audience results will be misclassified.

For SAML destination-binding tests, if the assertion status contains a Destination element, Dex requires it to exactly match redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST keep Destination consistent with redirectURI unless it is intentionally testing destination validation; otherwise login failure is expected setup failure, not a security finding.

Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. I4 principal-binding tests MUST vary NameID directly; changing only email or username attributes does not change the principal Dex binds to.

Because Dex binds identity to NameID, the saml_email_binding_collision attack should be interpreted carefully: differing email with the same NameID is by design not a collision, while differing NameID values are the relevant principal-binding input.

For I4 multi-identity tests, NameID matching is exact string identity from the assertion. There is no documented wildcard, regex, or glob mode for NameID. The fuzzer MUST send distinct literal NameID values for collision/case/unicode tests and MUST NOT assume '*' or patterns have special meaning.

Dex SAML group filtering is exact-membership based on allowedGroups. There is no documented companion parameter enabling glob or regex matching for allowedGroups. For multi-identity scenarios requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups entirely rather than set wildcard-like values.

If filterGroups=true, Dex excludes any groups not present in allowedGroups from the resulting claims. I5 group-policy tests MUST account for this claim-pruning behavior; missing groups after login may be by-design filtering rather than authorization loss or corruption.

Dex SAML connector does not support refresh tokens, and offline_access is ignored for this connector. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect refresh_token issuance in SAML authorization-code flows; absence of refresh_token is by design, not an I2 failure.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions, include a control flow that uses a valid SAML login through the same connector and client. Without a successful control, a failed forged assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated setup, callback mismatch, or connector misconfiguration.

Dex token exchange is documented only for OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt to use token_exchange as a SAML-upstream operation or interpret its absence/failure as a SAML vulnerability.

Dex configuration is file-based, and the documented management API is gRPC rather than HTTP REST. The provided docs do not document HTTP endpoints for enabling connectors, creating policies, seeding resources, revoking sessions, or dynamically modifying SAML connector config. The fuzzer MUST treat these operations as absent from the documented HTTP API for this profile.

Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST begin with start_oidc_auth and preserve the returned state/RelayState flow so Dex can issue an AuthnRequest; Dex validates InResponseTo and will reject unsolicited SAML responses.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Overview: dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the response's InResponseTo value.

saml.constraint: For I1 signature-validation default tests, Dex documentation explicitly states insecureSkipSignatureValidation skips signature validation and should only be used for testing. A valid security test of Dex defaults MUST leave insecureSkipSignatureValidation unset/false; setting it true creates an intentional insecure configuration, not a product vulnerability.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Configuration: insecureSkipSignatureValidation true skips signature validation.

saml.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer when testing issuer mismatch. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex may have no explicit expected Issuer value to compare against, so an issuer-mismatch result is ambiguous. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'issuer check not configured' from 'issuer check bypassed'.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Configuration: Optional Issuer value expected in the SAML response.

saml.constraint: For I5 audience tests, redirectURI is the expected audience for AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified; if entityIssuer is set, it overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST craft SAML Audience values against entityIssuer when present, otherwise against redirectURI, or it will misclassify audience-validation behavior.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Configuration: redirectURI used as expected audience if entityIssuer isn't specified; entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as required audience.

saml.constraint: For I5 destination tests, if the SAML response/assertion status contains a Destination element, it must exactly match redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST keep Destination aligned with redirectURI except when intentionally testing destination validation, otherwise failures are setup errors.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Configuration: Destination element must match redirectURI exactly.

saml.constraint: Dex uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. I4 principal-binding tests MUST vary NameID to test identity uniqueness; changing only email/username while keeping NameID constant is by design expected to map to the same Dex user.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Overview and Configuration: NameID is mapped to user ID; nameIDPolicyFormat should ensure uniqueness and stability.

saml.constraint: For I4 email-binding-collision tests, Dex documentation says NameID, not emailAttr or usernameAttr, is the unique identifier. A login where NameID=attacker and email=victim@example.com mapping to the attacker identity is BY DESIGN; only a merge based on email despite differing NameID would indicate a bug.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Overview: connector uses NameID as the user's unique identifier; attributes map to user info.

saml.constraint: For I2 replay tests, SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect refresh_token issuance or refresh-based replay/freshness behavior from SAML logins; use assertion replay patterns instead.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Caveats and connectors/_index.md: SAML connector supports no refresh tokens; offline_access ignored.

saml.constraint: For I2 assertion replay tests, include a control authorization-code exchange after a valid SAML login. A failure at token exchange may stem from Dex authRequests code lifetime expiry rather than SAML assertion rejection. The fuzzer SHOULD compare a valid fresh flow against the replayed assertion flow.
saml.source: configuration/tokens.md expiry.authRequests defines time frame to exchange a code; connectors/saml.md describes SAML login flow.

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel analysis: no SAML-specific numeric sentinel values are documented for this protocol surface. However Dex duration fields use explicit duration strings (number+unit such as 10m). The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0, 0s, or -1 disable SAML/OAuth checks unless explicitly documented in the active config, because the provided docs do not define such sentinels for SAML-related expiry settings.
saml.source: configuration/tokens.md: duration options use number+time unit; no 0/-1 sentinel semantics documented for SAML.

saml.constraint: For I5 group-filter tests, allowedGroups is exact list-membership against groups extracted from groupsAttr; filterGroups=true only removes non-allowed groups from the emitted claim set. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat allowedGroups as wildcard/regex matching, and MUST distinguish 'authentication requires membership in at least one allowed group' from 'extra groups are filtered out of claims'.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios involving groups, groupsAttr names the SAML attribute to read and groupsDelim only splits a single string into multiple groups. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume alternate type coercions like string vs array are equivalent unless it controls groupsDelim and attribute encoding; otherwise type-confusion results may reflect encoding differences, not identity bugs.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md Configuration: groupsAttr and groupsDelim semantics.

saml.constraint: For SAML freshness/replay tests, use the same SAML assertion twice in two saml_login events within the same SP-initiated flow shape. Dex documentation states it persists state for preventing replays, so replay outcomes are meaningful for SAML assertions; unlike stateless JWT replay, a second acceptance is security-relevant here.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores the offline_access scope. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token after SAML login as a bug, and do NOT build SAML test sequences that depend on refresh-token issuance or revocation.

For I1 signature-validation default tests, the fuzzer MUST account for Dex's documented insecure testing switch insecureSkipSignatureValidation. If the deployment enables this option, acceptance of attacker-signed SAMLResponse is by configuration and not a product flaw. A valid insecure-default test requires the option to be absent, not explicitly enabled.

For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer when possible. The docs mark ssoIssuer as optional expected Issuer value in the SAML response; if it is unset, issuer comparison may be skipped or rely on weaker defaults, so an issuer-mismatch acceptance would be ambiguous. To test issuer enforcement correctly, set ssoIssuer to the trusted IdP entity ID and then send idp_entity_id with a different value.

For I5 audience tests, configure entityIssuer explicitly when possible. Dex uses redirectURI as the expected AudienceRestriction audience if entityIssuer is not specified, but entityIssuer overrides that audience when present. The fuzzer MUST compare against the actual configured expected audience; otherwise a wrong-audience test may target the wrong SP entity and misclassify results.

For I5 no-conditions and wrong-audience tests, remember that if the SAML response contains a Destination element it must match redirectURI exactly. A rejection caused by Destination mismatch is not evidence that Conditions or AudienceRestriction were enforced. Keep Destination aligned with redirectURI while varying only Conditions/Audience fields.

For I4 identity-collision tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. The fuzzer MUST vary NameID to test principal binding. Changing only email or username attributes while keeping NameID constant is expected to map to the same principal and is not an identity-collision bug.

For I4 email-binding-collision tests, use NameID and email independently. Dex maps assertion attributes like email/username to user info, but NameID is the unique identifier. Therefore a login with NameID=attacker and email=victim@example.com should not be judged as a collision unless downstream identity binding follows email instead of NameID.

For SAML group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is list-membership exact matching against SAML group values; the docs do not describe wildcard, glob, or regex matching for allowedGroups itself. For multi-identity scenarios, if multiple different group values must pass the same connector, OMIT allowedGroups rather than setting '*' or regex-like strings, which would be treated as literal group names.

groupsDelim changes parsing semantics for groupsAttr: without it, multiple groups are expected as repeated attributes; with it, a single string is split by the delimiter. For I4 type-confusion and I5 group-authorization tests, keep this setting fixed and intentional, because changing it alters whether one string becomes many groups and can create false positives.

For I2 expired/future assertion tests, include a control login in the same environment using a valid SAML assertion alongside the attack login. Otherwise a failed SAML login cannot be distinguished from generic connector misconfiguration such as bad CA, wrong redirectURI/Destination, or missing SP-initiated state.
